problem: Prior audio-visual navigation (AV-Nav, AV-WaN) handles only a single static sound source in clean audio, generalizes poorly to unheard sounds, is brittle to distractors/noise, and does not cover moving sources.
motivation: Real robots must follow moving sources such as people or pets, and must work amid distractors and noisy audio. Existing architectures also encode audio and geometry separately and never learn a spatial fusion of the two. Training on only 73 heard sounds leads to overfitting.
key_idea: Fuse the binaural spectrogram into the geometric occupancy map via a learned spatial audio encoder (early fusion), train with randomized complex audio scenarios (second source, distractors, SpecAugment), and introduce a dynamic moving-source benchmark with the DSPL metric.
insight: Training with complex audio scenarios (second sound at goal, distractors, spectrogram masking) is the largest driver of generalization to unheard sounds; it lifts all models, e.g. Ours unheard SPL on Replica 48.6->54.0. The decomposition ablation shows different components help on different datasets, so combining them is needed. A 3x3 action map (fewer ignored observations) speeds up learning, which matters in dynamic settings. The spectrogram-reconstruction auxiliary task helps unheard Replica but not MP3D, and hurts heard sounds.
method: Spatial Audio Encoder: transposed convolutions upsample the binaural spectrogram (2x65x69 Replica / 2x65x26 MP3D) to the 2x200x200 geometric map size
Audio-Visual Encoder: concatenates the upsampled audio features with the allocentric occupancy/explored map G_map built from depth, then 3 conv layers + FC to a 512-d embedding
Policy: GRU (512) memory with linear actor/critic, trained end-to-end with PPO; also uses a separate audio encoder and depth encoder; reward +10 success, ±0.25 dense distance shaping, -0.01 per step
Action parametrization: waypoint selection on a reduced 3x3 action map (vs 9x9 in AV-WaN), executed by a Dijkstra planner
Dynamic AudioGoal benchmark: the source follows shortest paths to random goals and moves with probability 0.7 per step; new metrics DSPL/DSNA use the earliest possible intercept as the oracle

Complex audio scenarios pipeline: per-episode random second sound at the goal, per-step random distractor sounds at random locations, and random time/frequency masking of the spectrogram, all from training sounds only

setting.backbone: Custom CNN encoders + GRU actor-critic (PPO), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: RL in SoundSpaces on Replica (9/4/5 scenes) and Matterport3D (59/10/12 scenes) with 102 sounds split 73/11/18; augmented with second sounds, distractors, SpecAugment; dynamic training uses 50% moving-source episodes
setting.observation: Depth image (projected into occupancy map) + binaural spectrogram; no goal vector
setting.action_space: Waypoint on 3x3 local action map executed by a Dijkstra planner (low-level MoveForward/Rotate/Stop)
setting.privileged: none (the DSPL metric uses oracle path information for evaluation only)

numbers_note: Split labels: the paper reports the test split of SoundSpaces (heard/unheard) without naming it explicitly; only unheard rows are listed. Heard-sound results and Replica complex-eval rows are also in the tables. Challenge-set numbers are given only as percentage-point gains.
results: On static unheard AudioGoal, the architecture alone raises SR from 51.1 (AV-Nav) to 63.6 on Replica and from 56.6 (AV-WaN) to 60.6 on MP3D. With complex scenarios, SPL goes from 27.3 to 54.0 (Replica) and from 39.6 to 55.0 (MP3D) relative to AV-WaN. On the dynamic task it reaches SR 93.1/95.0 on heard sounds and 68.0/74.0 on unheard with complex training. It also won the CVPR 2021 SoundSpaces Challenge.
limitations: Sound sources have no embodiment or semantics, and the sound plays continuously; evaluated only in simulation, with no real-robot test
SoundSpaces gives BRIRs only at discrete grid points, which precludes continuous actions, intermediate locations and actuation noise (continuous-action attempt performed worse)
Complex training hurts heard-sound performance on small Replica scenes, and results are inconsistent across datasets
